title: Describing Routes and City Movement
summary: Explaining directions, routes, and movement through the city.
whyItMatters: Good directions use visible landmarks, ordered steps, transport details, and a clear final arrival point.

mentalModel.title: Orient, sequence, confirm
mentalModel.content: Identify the starting point, give one step at a time, and confirm the destination.

mentalModel.title: Use landmarks at decisions
mentalModel.content: Mention a visible place where the listener must turn, cross, or change transport.

ruleBlocks.title: Confirm the starting point
ruleBlocks.content: Ask where the person is now and which direction they are facing.

ruleBlocks.title: Give short ordered instructions
ruleBlocks.content: Use zuerst, dann, danach, bis, and schließlich with one action per step.

ruleBlocks.title: Check understanding
ruleBlocks.content: Ask whether the line, transfer, landmark, or final street is clear.

examples.de: Gehen Sie zuerst geradeaus bis zur Ampel.
examples.en: First go straight ahead to the traffic light.

examples.de: Nehmen Sie die U2 Richtung Pankow und steigen Sie am Alexanderplatz aus.
examples.en: Take the U2 toward Pankow and get off at Alexanderplatz.

examples.de: Das Museum liegt direkt gegenüber vom Rathaus.
examples.en: The museum is directly opposite city hall.

commonMistakes.wrong: Give several turns in one long sentence.
commonMistakes.correct: Separate the route into numbered or sequenced steps.
commonMistakes.reason: Short steps are easier to follow.

commonMistakes.wrong: Name a transit line without its direction.
commonMistakes.correct: Add Richtung plus the terminal or destination.
commonMistakes.reason: The line number alone is ambiguous.

comparisons.summary: The theme supplies transport and service-disruption vocabulary.
Case choice distinguishes where something is from where it goes.
